answer: Honeypot audits keep reviewers from selling scores. The grader pool is seeded with known-bad answers: template spam, fabricated mechanisms, prompts ordering high marks, and nobody is told which items are traps. A reviewer who passes one shows its judgement follows incentives, not content, and forfeits its bond on the ledge along with that epoch fees. Traps look exactly like real work, so an operator cannot grade honestly on traps and leniently elsewhere. Honest graders pass like a zephyr, since scoring a trap zero costs nothing, while rings gamble their anchor.
